title: RWB-S8-E1065-APP: the deviation slice of the sandbox has no published case-reference source, no deviation count per case or per code, no operation or field names for the stage contract read, no codes or owner roles for R-DEV-05 and R-DEV-06, no test level for the ten legacy cases and an empty H row for eight patterns
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R6, R7.2, R7.3 and R9; context pack S8 rwb-deviation; split plan story line RWB-S8-E1065-APP; legacy RWB-E1-065; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.4, A2.5, A2.12 and A2.14; TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 T3.0 to T3.3, T4, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 slides 3, 4, 8 and 13; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8
section: Metadata (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies, External dependencies); Sections 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12.1 to 12.9, 13, 16 and 19
description: (1) The legacy sandbox seeded 92 tables in one `recovery` schema from one project; in the target `deviation` is S8's single table and no service may seed or read another service's tables, while the case estate (recovery_case, case_account, case_party) belongs to rwb-case, the documents to rwb-document and the interaction ledger to rwb-source-data, so the case references a seeded deviation attaches to have no published source and no contract read of rwb-case exists on this slice. (2) No source publishes how many deviations a case carries, the count per code, or the shape-to-code mapping beyond the deceased customer (X3) and the bankruptcy (X5). (3) The operation name, the path suffixes and the field names of the stage, seed-profile, database and role and failure contract are not published, and the read-only role `rwb_sandbox_read` and its grants are delivered by RWB-P1-E1065-DB, which is outside this story's X row. (4) The pattern set carries DP-03, DP-04, DP-07, DP-15 and DP-19, whose DP table rows add six platform H dependencies and one C dependency (RWB-P3-E1043-CON), while the plan's H row is empty and its C row holds only RWB-P1-E1065-CON. (5) The codes and owner roles of R-DEV-05 and R-DEV-06 are not printed by any source read for the slice. (6) The ten legacy test cases carry no level. (7) The dictionary tags no `deviation` column `is_personal`, so the scope of the personal-data pattern scan is a design choice. (8) The legacy criteria AC1 to AC9 are owned by RWB-P1-E1065-APP while the deviation half of several of them has to be proved in this service, which this story does with new criteria and no legacy AC.
evidence: Context pack S8 ownership rows (Tables 1 deviation, REST 2, Events EV-06 and EV-07, Jobs 0, Workflows 1); TSD S8 T3.1 deviation with DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045 and no foreign key outside the schema; TSD S8 T3.2 three lists; TSD S8 T4 22 rules over 9 states with R-DEV-05 and R-DEV-06 on DEV_FLAGGED and OWNER_ASSIGNED; FSD S8 A2.4.3.1 printing R-DEV-02 and R-DEV-03 only; FSD S8 A2.12 X3 deceased and A2.14 X5 bankruptcy; Architecture v5 slide 8 (X3 paused with contact stopped); legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 3, 4, 5, 8, 11, 12, 13, 16 and BR1 to BR9, AC1 to AC9; split plan RWB-S8-E1065-APP with acs empty, H empty, C RWB-P1-E1065-CON and X empty; RWB-P1-E1065-APP section 11 handing the deviation rows to this story
area: Contract; data; seed profile; rules; test levels; platform dependencies
owner_role: Solution architect, with the rwb-deviation owner, the rwb-case and rwb-document owners, the rwb-source-data sandbox owner, the rule-set owner of the Deviations package, the ACE DB team lead and the QA lead
proposed: Publish a deviation seed profile in RWB-P1-E1065-CON that carries the case references, their shapes and their routed states as a fixture; publish the deviation count per case and the shape-to-code mapping with the seed profile; name the operation and field names of the stage contract read and put the read-only role and its grants in the DB story X row of every sandbox slice; record the platform contracts as template dependencies of S8 and keep the H row empty; publish the codes and owner roles of R-DEV-05 and R-DEV-06 with the package version; publish the test level of the ten legacy cases and split each case between RWB-P1-E1065-APP, RWB-P3-E1065-APP, RWB-P5-E1065-APP, RWB-S8-E1065-APP and RWB-ITG-E1065-ITG
